summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition snapshot **22w13a**.  
2. Open a Singleplayer world with default settings.  
3. Use a teleport command (e.g. ``/tp @p <coordinates>``) to move several thousand blocks away to a structure that can naturally generate allays, such as a woodland mansion or pillager outpost, and land inside that structure.  
4. Press **F3** to open the debug screen and look at the chunk‑loading indicators to see if nearby chunks are loading.  
5. Press **F3 + A** to reload chunks.  
6. Wait a few seconds.  
7. Observe that chunks still do not load, UI menus open but do nothing, and the F3 screen shows the internal server tick stuck at **18 ms**.  
8. Open the **Esc** menu, select **Save and Quit to Title**, and watch the “Saving world…” screen.  
9. Observe that the saving process never finishes and commands (including further ``/tp`` or ``/locatebiome``) have no effect, leaving the game unresponsive.  
10. Take a screenshot of the F3 debug screen showing the stuck tick and note the observed hang.
Observed Behavior: When a player teleports several thousand blocks away to a structure that contains naturally generated allays, the server stops processing new chunks and the game becomes unresponsive; the F3 debug screen remains open but its internal server tick value freezes at roughly 18 ms, UI elements such as the gamemode selector open without responding, and commands no longer execute. Chunk loading does not resume even after forcing a reload with F3 A, and only a few chunks (typically two to eight) may appear if the player is positioned outside the allay‑bearing structure. Attempting to save the world while the hang persists leaves the “Saving world…” screen indefinitely, requiring the player to forcibly terminate the Java process, which results in no data being written. The issue is exclusive to naturally generated allays inside structures; summoning an allay with /summon allay or visiting a woodland mansion that lacks allays does not trigger the freeze. The problem manifests on snapshot 22w13a and appears to be caused by a deadlock that occurs when the game queries a chunk that is still generating during entity position updates, preventing the chunk from completing its generation and halting the server thread.
Expected Behavior: After teleporting to a distant structure that may contain naturally generated allays, the client should continue loading surrounding chunks normally, the F3 debug screen should update with the current tick rate, UI elements and commands should respond, and the server should remain responsive. The player should be able to move, switch gamemodes, and save or quit the world without hanging or requiring a forced crash.
